subject: calling STAN as a black box

messages.author: 2f65579495b33f0f
messages.subject: calling STAN as a black box
parts:
Hi all,

I'm interested in using STAN as a component of a much more complicated sampler.  My intended model has a nonparametric Bayesian hierarchy. It has lots of discrete assignments, and so representing things entirely as continuous parameters isn't possible. However, there are some non-conjugate updates to continuous parameters that I think STAN would be great for, since it has (1) fast C code, and (2) good mixing via NUTS.

Is it possible to use STAN in this way? To be concrete, suppose I have fixed data, discrete variables "Z" that I need to sample using my own custom methods, and continuous variables "theta" that I want STAN to sample. Ideally, the pseudocode (in high-level syntax) would look something like
 
for iter = 1:Niter
Z = SampleMyCustomDiscreteParams( data, theta ) 
theta = SampleContinuousParamsViaSTAN(  data,  Z, theta)
end

Right now, it looks like I could define a STAN model for theta given fixed Z,data.  This could be compiled, and called from my larger sampler as a "black box".  However,  this "black box" would write output to a csv file, and I'd have to do expensive file IO to get the samples back into my program.  Is there a way to bypass the "write to CSV" part of stan and have it return values directly?  I recognize this probably isn't easy, but hoping it might be possible.

Alternatively, I suppose I could try to directly implement the NUTS algorithm for the task at hand, but it seems a shame to reinvent the wheel when the code for STAN has been optimized and crafted so carefully.

Thanks for any help!
Mike

We've been thinking about similar issues for blocking
HMC parameters, adding Gibbs, etc. So far, there's not
an easy mechanism for doing this.

> Is it possible to use STAN in this way? To be concrete, suppose I have fixed data, discrete variables "Z" that I need to
> sample using my own custom methods, and continuous variables "theta" that I want STAN to sample. Ideally, the pseudocode
> (in high-level syntax) would look something like
> for iter = 1:Niter
>
> Z = SampleMyCustomDiscreteParams( data, theta )
>
> theta = SampleContinuousParamsViaSTAN( data, Z, theta)
>
> end
>
> Right now, it looks like I could define a STAN model for theta given fixed Z,data. This could be compiled, and called
> from my larger sampler as a "black box".
Hopefully we can be a bit more transparent than that.

> However, this "black box" would write output to a csv file, and I'd have to
> do expensive file IO to get the samples back into my program. Is there a way to bypass the "write to CSV" part of stan
> and have it return values directly? I recognize this probably isn't easy, but hoping it might be possible.

Check out the C++ generated when a Stan model is compiled
via stanc. This has some methods in it that you can use,
including one to write the parameters into a std::vector<double>
without going through file I/O (that's how the R interface works
without invoking file I/O).

Then you should treat the custom sampler as producing data
for the Stan model. You'd have to write something yourself
to read the data in.

One issue is how adaptation would work in this setting.
NUTS is set up to use the warmup samples to tune the
step sizes. This might still work with changing "data".
We haven't tried it yet with a combined discrete sampler.

> Alternatively, I suppose I could try to directly implement the NUTS algorithm for the task at hand, but it seems a shame
> to reinvent the wheel when the code for STAN has been optimized and crafted so carefully.

There's also the auto-dif. NUTS is easy in terms of
implementation compared to the variable transforms plus
auto-dif.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] calling STAN as a black box
parts:
The parameters are a std::vector and the
data's a sequence of structured member variables.
You can map a std::vector, but the structured
variables are going to be tricky unless you're
a real C++ memory-tweaking wizard.

- Bob
